sourceEvidence.title: PM-KISAN Operational Guidelines (revised 29.03.2020)
sourceEvidence.issuer: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
facts: Landholder farmer family is husband, wife and minor children owning cultivable land as per State/UT land records.
Benefit stated as ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments, subject to exclusions.

Exclusions include institutional landholders; specified constitutional/public representatives; serving or retired government employees subject to stated MTS/Class IV/Group D exceptions; pensioners with monthly pension ₹10,000 or more subject to stated exceptions; income-tax payers in the last assessment year; specified registered practising professionals; and NRIs for new beneficiaries.
Guideline contains a 01.02.2019 eligibility cut-off with inheritance-on-death and other land-transfer provisions.

sourceEvidence.title: Cabinet approval — continuation of PM-KISAN 2026–27 to 2030–31
sourceEvidence.issuer: Press Information Bureau / Cabinet / Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
facts: The Union Cabinet approved continuation of PM-KISAN from FY 2026–27 through FY 2030–31 with a ₹3.15 lakh crore outlay.
The release reiterates ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments for eligible farmer families; it does not announce a replacement operational guideline or change the 2020 eligibility clauses.
The continuation announcement must be read with any subsequent operational guideline, amendment or State/UT implementation circular before approval.

sourceEvidence.title: PM-KISAN current portal notice — 24th instalment and eKYC
sourceEvidence.issuer: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / Government of India
facts: The 24th instalment was released on 30 October 2026: over ₹18,690 crore to 9.34 crore farmers.
The release reiterates ₹6,000 annually in three equal ₹2,000 instalments, subject to eligibility, land-record seeding, Aadhaar-linked bank account and eKYC.
The release describes OTP, biometric and face-authentication eKYC routes and the State-led beneficiary identification/verification process.

The PM-KISAN portal separately flags suspected post-01.02.2019 land acquisitions and multiple family-member claims for temporary withholding pending physical verification; treat this as a manual verification trigger, not automatic ineligibility.

eligibilityMatrix.condition: Eligible landholding farmer family with cultivable land in State/UT records
eligibilityMatrix.implementation: Occupation keyword plus user-declared cultivable-land boolean
eligibilityMatrix.gap: Occupation is not a statutory eligibility condition by itself; family composition, land record ownership and State/UT validation are not captured.
eligibilityMatrix.reviewerAction: Decide whether the occupation field must be removed from eligibility logic and define the evidence/authority needed for land records.

eligibilityMatrix.condition: Family definition: husband, wife and minor children
eligibilityMatrix.gap: Cannot establish whether landholding and exclusion rules apply at family level.
eligibilityMatrix.reviewerAction: Specify family aggregation, separated-family and adult-child edge cases from current circulars.

eligibilityMatrix.gap: The rule does not enumerate or validate any exclusion class, threshold, exception or NRI condition.
eligibilityMatrix.reviewerAction: Build a clause-by-clause exclusion matrix with exact exceptions and evidence sources.

eligibilityMatrix.implementation: No acquisition date, succession or transfer fields
eligibilityMatrix.gap: Current portal explicitly flags certain post-cut-off land acquisition cases for physical verification.
eligibilityMatrix.reviewerAction: Reconcile all amendments and current portal instructions; define whether these cases always return needs_verification.

eligibilityMatrix.condition: State/UT identification, eKYC and beneficiary status
eligibilityMatrix.implementation: No authoritative integration; eKYC only a next-action message
eligibilityMatrix.gap: Cannot confirm State/UT approval, eKYC, bank validation or current beneficiary status.
eligibilityMatrix.reviewerAction: Keep official verification mandatory and avoid collecting Aadhaar/bank details in JanaSetu.

Confirm whether the 2026–27 to 2030–31 continuation has been accompanied by a revised operational guideline or only continuation of the existing scheme.
Verify the exact current eKYC methods, biometric exception paths, land-record cut-off implementation, succession/transfer cases, duplicate-family policy and State/UT exceptions.
Treat the portal’s suspected-case temporary withholding notice as a manual verification trigger, not an automatic ineligibility rule.
